content: Studies have indicated that certain antiarrhythmic drugs may increase the risk of death, particularly in individuals who have experienced a prior heart attack. This warning may also apply to quinidine. Quinidine is typically reserved for the treatment of life-threatening arrhythmias. Quinidine is prescribed to manage abnormal heart rhythms. It functions by increasing the heart's resistance to irregular electrical activity. Additionally, quinidine is used to treat malaria. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further information. Quinidine is available in tablet form for oral administration. Immediate-release quinidine is generally taken three or four times daily, while extended-release (long-acting) quinidine is usually taken two or three times daily. Extended-release tablets should not be cut, crushed, or chewed; they must be swallowed whole. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist to clarify any part you do not understand. Take quinidine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Quinidine helps control your condition but does not cure it. Continue taking quinidine even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking quinidine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to quinidine, quinine, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antidepressants, cimetidine, codeine products, diltiazem, medications for heart disease or high blood pressure, medications for seizures, sleep, or infections, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have an infection or have a history of myasthenia gravis, heart, kidney, or liver disease, or muscle weakness. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking quinidine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform the surgeon or dentist that you are taking quinidine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by quinidine. Discuss with your doctor the use of cigarettes and caffeine-containing beverages, as these may increase heart irritability and interfere with quinidine's effectiveness. Do not switch brands of this medication without consulting your doctor. Avoid consuming grapefruit juice while taking quinidine. Do not alter the amount of salt in your diet without consulting your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Quinidine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: diarrhea, stomach pain or cramps, dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, fatigue, weakness, rash, vision changes, difficulty sleeping, or tremor. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: irregular heartbeat, chest pain, skin rash, hearing changes (e.g., ringing or hearing loss), vision changes (e.g., blurred vision or light sensitivity), or unusual bleeding or bruising. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store quinidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the appropriate disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor will need to monitor your response to quinidine. Take quinidine at the same time each day at evenly spaced intervals. Changing the timing of your doses can reduce the medication's effectiveness. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
